name: Paradise Cave
kicker: Dry cave on a wooden walkway
summary: Dry boardwalk cave: walk about a kilometre inside at Km 16, the park’s other half-day beside the boat. A buggy or a forest path covers about 1.6 kilometres, then about 500 metres to the mouth. The park charges an adult 270,000 VND, buggy included. Vietjet still prints 250,000 VND. Ask the gate which hours are posted for the one-kilometre walk.
getThere: Km 16, west Ho Chi Minh road. Minutes are check on arrival.
heroCaption: Visitors on the wooden walkway inside Paradise Cave

notice.title: Two prices, and no park clock for the short walk
notice.body: The park page says 270,000 VND for an adult, buggy included, and it does not state the one-kilometre gate hours. Vietjet still prints 250,000 VND and 06:30–17:00. Confirm both before you go.

body: This is the dry cave. Buy the ticket at the site, cross about 1.6 kilometres of forest by electric buggy or on foot, walk about 500 metres to the entrance, and follow a wooden path for about a kilometre. The park gives the cave a length of 31.4 kilometres, a height of 60 metres, and a width from 30 metres to 100 metres, with some sections to 150 metres. On that same page the one-kilometre walk goes through chambers it describes as up to 150 metres wide and 100 metres high. The park says a British cave expedition found the entrance in 2005. The adult price is 270,000 VND and it includes the buggy. A child from 1.1 metres to 1.3 metres pays 145,000 VND. Under 1.1 metres is free.

Do not use the seven-kilometre timetable as your clock. That tour starts at 08:00, kayaks an underground river the park describes as 60 to 100 metres across, reaches an opening it calls Heaven’s Well, and is back at the center about 16:00. It costs 2,000,000 VND and needs at least two people. The overnight version is 4,000,000 VND, needs at least five people, and the park closes it to children under 16 and to people with heart disease or high blood pressure. The park page does not say when the one-kilometre gate opens.

Keep this off the boat morning. The address is kilometre 16 on the west branch of the Ho Chi Minh road. The minutes from Phong Nha village are check on arrival. The 20 minutes the park prints for Mooc Spring is the drive from Phong Nha Cave to the spring, not to this gate.

figures.alt: A wooden walkway and stalactites inside Paradise Cave

gettingThere: Paradise Cave’s operator address is Km 16 on the west branch of the Ho Chi Minh road. Go by road from the village. No minute count was printed on the park page or on the Vietjet listing. The minutes are check on arrival.

legs.heading: From Phong Nha village
legs.body: By road to Km 16, west Ho Chi Minh road. The park does not publish the minutes. Check them on arrival.

closed: No weekly closing day is published for the 1 km walk. Confirm the gate on arrival.
admissionNote: Park page, adult 270,000 VND, including the entrance and the electric buggy. Child from 1.1 m to 1.3 m, 145,000 VND with the buggy. Under 1.1 m free. Vietjet’s destination page prints 250,000 VND and daily hours of 06:30–17:00. The two pages disagree, so both figures stay. The park page does not state the one-kilometre gate hours. The 7 km one-day tour is 2,000,000 VND, minimum two people, starts at 08:00, and the park’s timetable ends about 16:00. It kayaks a river the park describes as 60 to 100 metres across and finishes at Heaven’s Well. It is not the boardwalk ticket. The overnight tour is 4,000,000 VND, minimum five people, and is closed to children under 16 and to people the page lists with heart disease or high blood pressure.
